name: ASTM F2291 acceleration limits as the public sources give them
edition: F2291-23b (curves, as Rohde 2024 redraws them); rules also from F2291-06a (2006)
edition_note: TRANSCRIBED FROM PUBLIC SECONDARY SOURCES, not from the standard, and not checked against any edition of it. The curves describe F2291-23b as Rohde (2024) redraws it, with Cargill (2019) and the publisher's preview of F2291-21 as second sources; several rules are confirmed by the 2006 edition's text (F2291-06a). The current edition is F2291-26b. Research notes: docs/research/r3-force-limits.md (R3) and docs/research/r13-force-limits-second-sources.md (R13).
disclaimer: A design aid for a hobby tool, not a certification. A pass means only: within the limits as transcribed here, at the points the program models.
how_to_check: Every number below has an id, a source and a confidence, and a field 'checked' that is null. When you have compared a number with your own copy of the standard, correct the value if needed and replace null with a short text: the edition and where you found it, and the date, for example "F2291-26b Fig. 8, 2026-12-01". The program then reports that number's confidence as 'checked'. Leave 'source' as it is. A number the sources leave open has the value null. fvdcore limits --file <this file> shows the file as the program reads it.

confidence_scale: high: two independent sources agree; medium: one good source; low: read off one drawing only, a weak source, or an FVD++ choice. A number whose 'checked' is filled in is reported as 'checked'.

interpolation: straight lines in g against s between points; the first value from min_event_s to the first point; after the last point the last value holds (or the 'then' curve applies) up to max_duration_s, and beyond it the value at max_duration_s

base.name: base case (lap bar or similar, Class 4 or 5)

restraint_kinds.source: N6 (F2291-06a 7.1.4.7: the three basic restraint types; Figs. 11 to 18 titled x 'Base/OTS' and x 'Prone' for the eggs); R Fig. 7.2; C Fig. 6 (the three -Gx lines)
restraint_kinds.note: The aliases map the train catalogue's restraint words: lap bar, vest, other and none take the base case (FVD: R13 calls a lap bar without shoulder restraint the base case an inference; vest is not covered by any source).

combination.rule: quarter-ellipse per quadrant on the filtered instantaneous values: (a/A)^2 + (b/B)^2 <= 1, centred at (0,0); A and B are the min_event_s limits of the curve for each component's sign times radius_factor (the -x radius from the restraint kind's egg_x_neg_curve, the -z radius from z_neg, or from z_neg_extended when the extended line is allowed)

radii.source: R sec. 7.2.8.2, Table 7.1, formulas (1)-(3); N6 (F2291-06a 7.1.5.1, figure titles: z 'Base', z 'Extended', y 'Base')

pairs.source: R sec. 7.2.8.2, Table 7.1, formulas (1)-(3), Fig. 7.15; C (the standard's Fig. 11, edition not stated); N6 (F2291-06a 7.1.5.1)

radius_factor.source: R sec. 7.2.8.2 (no factor in R's account of F2291-23b); N6 (F2291-06a 7.1.5.1: radii are the 200 ms limits x 1.1)
radius_factor.note: CONTRADICTED between sources (R13 item 7): the 2006 edition has 1.1, Rohde's account of 23b has none. 1.0 is the stricter reading (decision record 0014 point 9). Your copy settles it.

sustained_s.source: FVD: an egg is judged on the value held for at least this long (the same 0.2 s below which the standard does not address impacts), so a spike shorter than that is not a finding

combination.three_axis: Rohde's (ax/A)^2 + (ay/B)^2 + (az/C)^2 <= 1 is in neither standard (R formula (4)); not encoded

event_threshold_g.source: FVD: an event in one direction is a stretch at or beyond this value (one slice step), so noise around zero does not split it

reversal_xy.note: A 2023 ballot was to reword this clause after 23b (R13 item 12), so the current text may differ. Each event's peak is its largest value; of equal values, the one nearest the other event (the stricter reading). The halved limit is that direction's limit at min_event_s. A stricter peak-to-peak criterion (R pp.44-45) is not adopted; not encoded.

restraint_areas.rule: From the trace filtered at restraint_filter. A point belongs to the lowest area whose region contains it or lies within line_tolerance_g of it (on a boundary the lower area may be chosen: A, F2291-21 Fig. 2 note 1). Each region below is that area together with every lower one; outside region 4 is area 5. Information only: the area says which restraint class the ride needs; it is not a pass or fail.
restraint_areas.source: A (F2291-21 Fig. 2, 6.4.3.2, 6.4.3.3); C; R Fig. 6.1 (all three agree); N6 Fig. 2 (grid values)
restraint_areas.confidence_rule: Each region has its own confidence: high when its corners are all grid values (two sources agree), at most medium when a corner is marked approximate (read to +-0.05 g), low when a corner is marked open (not legible in any source). The loader refuses a region rated higher than its corners allow. The 20 g corners only close the regions (FVD).
